content: 1. If sensitization or severe local irritation occurs with the use of Altabax (retapamulin), the treatment should be discontinued immediately. The ointment should be removed, and an appropriate alternative therapy for the infection should be initiated. 2. Altabax is not intended for systemic use or application on mucosal surfaces. It should not be ingested or used orally, intranasally, ophthalmically, or intravaginally. The safety and efficacy of Altabax on mucosal surfaces have not been established. Cases of epistaxis (nosebleeds) have been reported when Altabax was applied to nasal mucosa. 3. The use of antibiotics, including Altabax, may promote the growth of organisms that are not susceptible to the drug. If a superinfection occurs during treatment, appropriate measures should be taken. Prescribing Altabax in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. 4. In studies on pregnant rats, retapamulin was administered orally at doses of 50, 150, or 450 mg/kg/day from days 6 to 17 of gestation. Maternal toxicity, such as reduced body weight gain and decreased food consumption, as well as developmental toxicity, including reduced fetal body weight and delayed skeletal ossification, were observed at doses of 150 mg/kg/day or higher. No treatment-related malformations were observed in fetal rats. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of Altabax in pregnant women. Because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response, Altabax should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefits outweigh the potential risks. 5. It is not known whether retapamulin is excreted in human breast milk. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when Altabax is administered to a nursing woman. The safety of retapamulin use during breastfeeding has not been established. 6. The safety and effectiveness of Altabax in treating impetigo have been established in pediatric patients aged 9 months to 17 years. This is supported by evidence from well-controlled clinical trials involving 588 pediatric subjects who received at least one dose of retapamulin ointment, 1%. The efficacy and safety profile in pediatric patients aged 9 months and older were similar to those observed in adults. However, the safety and effectiveness of Altabax in pediatric patients younger than 9 months have not been established. In an open-label clinical trial involving patients aged 2 to 24 months, systemic exposure to retapamulin was higher in younger pediatric subjects compared to older ones. The highest systemic exposure levels were observed in subjects aged 2 to 6 months. Therefore, the use of retapamulin is not indicated in pediatric patients younger than 9 months. 7. Among the subjects in the clinical trials of Altabax, 234 were aged 65 years and older, and 114 were aged 75 years and older. No overall differences in safety or effectiveness were observed between these older subjects and younger adult subjects.
